title: P7 refusal-direction bidirectional validation (ablate/induce + random controls) - Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
_what_this_is: Expected-cell manifest for the refusal-direction validation phase. NONE of the generic check_manifest keys apply to refval (rows carry no 'split'/'cell'/'window' column and no 'sid'/'id', and expected_arms would misfire because behav_arms() only parses behavioural arm columns). Coverage is enforced by check_refval, which requires every (family,layer) to carry all four intervention arms at paired-equal n against its baseline. The grid below documents the frozen expected (family x layer x arm) cells so a never-launched cell is distinguishable from a ran-and-null one.
_notes: Run-dir naming: refval_<cohort>_<ts>_<uniq>; resolved by the shorter-prefix rule; presence of this file alone clears the 'no manifest' warning.

expected_splits / min_n_per_split / expected_arms / expected_cells / expected_windows are ALL deliberately ABSENT: including any of them would make check_manifest raise a spurious MISSING (refval has no split/cell/window column, no sid/id, and its arm names are not behav-detectable). This mirrors the phase9 manifest's rationale for omitting expected_arms on a non-behavioural type.

layers and families are run-parameterized (--layers, --families). Values below are the canonical continuation set (--layers 9,16,18,21,22,30 --families existing,clearharm). Baseline arms base_harmful/base_benign are generated once with family=None,layer=None.

'existing' family is induce-tested in-sample (its directions were fit on the whole harmless list); 'clearharm' is out-of-sample. See script header. A refit 'existing_fit' family is planned, not yet run.

grid.pairing_contract: ablate n == ablate_rand n == base_harmful n; induce n == induce_rand n == base_benign n (check_refval enforces)
